title: Saving documents in Draft Mode
text:
Saving documents in Draft Mode 
 N avigation in Farvision 
 Saving documents in draft mode 
 Draft mode allows users to temporarily save typed data without storing the data in the actual transactional database. Large transactions can be saved in interim state as Draft mode for future use. User can resume re-entry of transactions from draft mode. 
 Transactions within draft mode are not available for any further subsequent processing. Draft Mode has to be set as ‘ON’ in the interface for Draft mode saving button to be enabled. There is no such setting required for Draft mode enabling. It is enabled by code only. 
 ‘Save As Draft’ is enabled under submit menu. 
 After a document is saved as draft, user can only retrieve it again after making draft mode on in the same interface. 
 Click on the row to open the screen and make further entry or necessary changes. After that user is required to finally submit and save the entry. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Queue Management for Reports
text:
Queue Management for Reports 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Queue Management for Reports 
 Queue management allows for processing of data in the background so that the user does not have to wait while data is being processed. Once the report or process is completed a notification will be provided that the job has been completed. It is important to use queues so that server utilization is not disturbed during peak working hours. 
 There are two types of queues 
 Queue Reports 
 Queue Processes 
 Notifications 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of job. Report can be downloaded from the notification alert. Queue Reports 
Some reports and bulk print format can be queued. There are two types of processes 
 ● Fire and forget - the queue is started on demand when the report has to be processed 
 ● Repeat every few minutes - any data which is added for the bulk processing will be processed, and checking for new data will be done on a predefined frequency. 
 Fire and forget 
 A job id is assigned against reports which are being queued under fire and forget. A notification will be sent to the user’s device once the report is ready. Reports which have been queued can only be printed from the Queue management console. Queued reports cannot be printed (either PDF or Excel) from the menu interface from which generation of report was started. 
 Example : Application detail register, Booking register, Invoice register and Receipt register, Indent register, Purchase order register, Goods receipt Note register and Purchase Bill register. Examples for Bulk Printing of documents are Invoice, Booking annexure, Applicant Ledger. 
 Repeat every few minutes 
Queues which repeat every few minutes are used for bulk printing of documents. No job id assigned as it is a continuous loop where more documents which are added for bulk processes are picked up. After receiving the notification, search Bulk Printing in the menu column and then for the relevant menu Item. 
 Download : Once the report is complete, it can be downloaded and saved locally. The report will be automatically deleted after downloading. Reports will be visible in the queue console until the reports are downloaded. Users are allowed to download their reports while admin users can download report of any user. 
 Delete : Pending and generated report can be deleted. If the status is pending, the delete button will stop the processing of the report. If the status is Complete, delete will physically remove the report and it will not be available, it is deleted from the server. 
 Status : Pending, In Process, Complete, Error, No record found are the status of the queued report. 
 Remarks : This column provides details of the status. Example, For In process, it will show start. 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of the job. Hide Downloaded : On select of the Hide Downloaded check box, all downloaded row items will be hidden and only those row items will be shown which are pending for download. Queue Process 
 Some reports a process has to be run before the report can be generated. 
 Example : Finance module cash flow report generated through process method and process report will be downloaded from queue console under the Process tab. 
 Property management invoice generated through bulk invoice menu after notification will be downloaded from the queue console. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Report Scheduler
text:
Report Scheduler 
 Some common features 
 of Farvision 
 Report Schedular 
 User 
 can schedule reports to be mailed to themselves or other users. User can 
 choose the frequency of emailing reports, and set date and time when the 
 reports will be emailed. 
 To schedule 
 a report, click on ‘Scheduler’ button and then click on ‘Create Scheduler’. 
 Email 
 Report: Select 
 the option ‘To Me and/or Other’ before adding users or ‘To Me’ to mail 
 the report to the user only. 
 Add/Filter 
 User : Select the user(s) who will receive the report in email by clicking 
 on the user name(s) in left pane. The name(s) will appear in the right 
 pane. To remove the user, user is required to click on the user name in 
 the right pane. 
 Type : 
 There are two types as ‘Run Once’ and ‘Recurring’ 
 If ‘Run Once’ option is 
 chosen then ‘Start Date’ and ‘Start Time’ are to be entered 
 If ‘Recurring’ option is 
 chosen then user is required to set the frequency and schedule the same 
 If ‘Frequency’ is chosen 
 as ‘Daily’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled On’ as ‘Every Day’ 
 or ‘Every Week Day(Mon-Fri)’ 
 If ‘Frequency’ is chosen 
 as ‘Weekly’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled Day’ in the week 
 If ‘Frequency’ is chosen 
 as ‘Monthly’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled Date’ in the 
 Month 
 If 
 ‘Frequency’ is chosen as ‘Hourly’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled 
 Hour’ 
 If 
 ‘Frequency’ is chosen as ‘Minutes’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled 
 Minute’

title: Data Import Process
text:
Data Import Process 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Data Import Process 
 Data import allows data to be imported from excel sheets instead of entering through the interface. Data has to be entered in pre-defined excel sheets, checked for correctness and is then imported into Farvision. Data import is available for many masters and a few transactions, the process of importing is the same. Only the excel template is different in which data has to be entered. 
 Data import is normally used by first time users of Farvision, or if there is a huge volume. Bulk data can be inserted into Farvision and it saves time. Once your backlog is cleared, it is recommended to use the interface for day to day entry. Sometimes data import is also used where the number of rows in a document is very large, example a journal voucher with 200 lines. 
 There are four steps to be followed 
 ● Download Template 
 ● Upload Template 
 ● Validate Data 
 ● Import Data 
 DOWNLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Object: This is the master or transaction form for which the excel template has to be downloaded. 
 Nested Objects: Some forms which have to be imported have a lot of data, and have multiple excel worksheets in one excel template. These multiple worksheets normally correspond to tabs of the entry interface. Example, Account Head Import will have the worksheets for Ledger, Ledger Address, Ledger Communication, Ledger Contact, Bank Details, etc. 
 All these worksheets are linked to each other through a common field called Link Ref Code . The same value of this field in each row has to be entered under ImportLinkRefCode in the nested worksheets. In the Ledger worksheet Link Ref Code ‘1’ has details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ has details of Amit Kumar Pal. In the Ledger Address worksheet, ImportLinkRefCode ‘1’ will contain address details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ will contain address details of Amit Kumar Pal. The value given to the Link Ref Code and ImportLinkRefCode has to be the same so that data in the different worksheets can be associated with each other. 
 Download template : Download the template by clicking the Download button. An excel file will be downloaded on your local computer. Open the excel sheet. Enter the data in the excel sheet. 
 About the Excel Template 
 There may be one or more worksheets in which data has to or can be entered. Click on the different worksheets to enter data in them. Remember to use the same identifying value in all worksheets so that data between the different worksheets can be linked to each other. In case there is no data to be filled in the nested worksheets, leave it blank. Do not fill only the ImportLinkRefCode if no other data is available for entry in that sheet. In case there is a row in the main sheet but there is no associated data for that row in the linked sheets, skip that row number in the linked sheet. 
 Each excel template has an Info worksheet which will guide the user about the properties of the fields. 
 Sheet Name : Worksheet names are listed here. 
 Column Names : Fields available in all associated worksheets are listed here. Data has to be entered as rows, fields are the columns. 
 Properties : Fields can have the following properties 
 Is required: True - this is a mandatory field, has to be entered. 
 Is required: False - this is an optional field. 
 Max length: The maximum number of characters which can be entered in that field. 
 The following points have to be kept in mind while filling data in the prescribed excel sheet 
 Do not remove any columns or worksheets , even if there is no data to be entered in them. Format must be as per the original excel template downloaded. 
 Do not change any names, settings, alignment, formatting of fields, worksheet, or files . 
 Remove any hyperlinks from the data fields . Example Email. 
 Try to import records into batches of 100, 200 or 500 rows at a time. Import can be run multiple times. Data will keep on getting added in Farvision. 
 Fill all mandatory fields 
 Enter data in ImportLinkRefCode if data is there in the associated worksheets 
 Do not enter blank rows , especially at the end of the excel sheet 
 Wherever applicable, Debit and Credit amounts should tally . 
 Spelling of account heads, parent account, items, etc should be correct, i.e. match with the masters in Farvision 
 Wherever applicable, data in related sheets should tally with the data in the main sheet . Example, Receipt/Payment or Journals, the Adjustment Info amount for each party should tally with the amount in Ledger details for the same party. 
 Some tips 
 Clear cache and clear history of the browser, in case of unknown error 
 UPLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Upload the filled out excel Template to start the data uploading process. 
 Select File : Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. 
 The template can be dragged and dropped or the same can be selected from its location. Click on the Drop files to upload panel. Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. Click on the Upload button. Once the template has been uploaded, it will show the message Uploaded Successfully. Click on Next button to go to the data validation step. VALIDATE DATA Once the filled up excel has been uploaded, the data has to be validated from the template and click on Next 
 Process Queue : Click on the box so that the validation process can be routed through the Queue Management console. If the data volume is large, it is important to queue this process else the server will become very slow. 
 Validate Data : Click on the Start Validation button to start the validation process. 
 Status : While the data validation is ongoing, a status bar will show Validating Data, Please Wait. If the data validation is successful, it will show the status as Success. If data is not correct and has failed the validation process, it will show Error Found. 
 Result : In case the status is not successful, the reasons why validation has failed will be provided in this Excel file which can be downloaded. The file will have both data which has a problem and data which is correct. The data where there is a problem is highlighted in yellow. The problems with the data will be displayed in the Import Remarks column. In this example, HSN Id does not exist for Construction service in HSN Master. 
 In this example, Relationship should have Son or Wife, and the name Rakesh Kumar and Mahaveer Singh should have been entered in Relative Name respectively. 
 In this example, Postal code is a mandatory field that can’t be blank. 
 The validation routine has to be run repeatedly till there are no errors left. 
 Click on the Next button to go to the Import Data tab. 
 IMPORT DATA 
 Click on Start Import to start importing data from filled up excel template file into Farvision. On successful import, it will show the status as Success. Click on the Finish button. Data which has been imported can be checked in the respective Advanced Search for the transaction or master forms. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Hierarchy Type
text:
Hierarchy Type 
 Help > Setup > Project" />
 Hierarchy 
 Type 
 What is Hierarchy Type? 
 Setting hierarchy in a real estate project 
 involves defining different levels such as Phase, Tower Group / Category 
 Group, Tower / Category, and Wing / Subcategory. This is done to organise 
 and structure the project’s elements. 
 Why do We Need to Create Hierarchy Types? 
 Having a clear hierarchy in a real estate 
 project helps in better management, organisation, and communication among 
 the project team members and stakeholders. It provides a structured framework 
 for decision-making, resource allocation, and tracking sales status at 
 various levels of the project. 
 When are Hierarchy Types Applicable? 
 Establishing the hierarchy should be 
 done early in the project planning and design stages for property sales. 
 This ensures a smooth and efficient workflow throughout the project's 
 lifecycle. 
 As the project progresses, regular reviews 
 of the hierarchy may be necessary to align it with updates in the sales 
 status. This helps maintain the structure of the project. 
 Use Case 
 Phase: When 
 dealing with a large plot of land for development, the process often involves 
 dividing the area into different sections, known as phases . This 
 approach is particularly beneficial for managing extensive projects and 
 ensuring systematic and organised development over time. 
 Tower Group or Category Group: 
 Within each of these phases, multiple 
 towers or buildings are constructed, which are collectively organised 
 into what is referred to as a tower group or category group . 
 For example, a collection of premium towers and standard towers within 
 a phase is known as a tower group or category group. This grouping allows 
 for better management of the different types of towers being developed. 
 Tower or Category: Now, within these tower groups, developers 
 often create a segregation between premium towers and standard towers 
 (example) to cater to the diverse preferences and budgets of potential 
 customers. This is what is known as tower or category . 
 Wing or Subcategory: At this level, there is an additional 
 layer of segregation based on the unit types, creating wings or subcategories. 
 For example, a “Premium 2 BHK subcategory” may offer larger, more luxurious 
 2 BHK units, while a “Standard 2 BHK subcategory” may provide more affordable 
 2 BHK options. 
 Hierarchy 
 Types are system generated. Units 
 will be always under Wing/Sub category level i.e. lowest/smallest level, 
 not at any higher level. 
 Defaults 
 values are –

 Schedule 
 Schedule 
 is a powerful tool which enables developers 
 to set and manage key milestones throughout a project. These milestones 
 are critical checkpoints marking significant phases and activities from 
 start to finish. By integrating these schedules into the system, developers 
 can ensure that everyone involved—investors, contractors, and property 
 owners/clients—is kept up to date on the project's progress. This transparency 
 improves coordination, accountability, and decision-making, leading to 
 more efficient project management and successful outcomes. 
 Why Create a Schedule for any Project? 
 Enhanced 
 Communication: All 
 stakeholders, including contractors, investors, and future residents, 
 can access the schedule through the ERP software, ensuring everyone 
 is informed about the project's progress and upcoming phases. 
 Improved Coordination: Contractors can plan their work and 
 allocate resources more effectively, knowing the exact timelines for 
 each milestone. 
 Transparency: 
 Investors can monitor the project's 
 progression, increasing their confidence and satisfaction with the 
 development process. 
 Risk 
 Management: Potential 
 delays or issues can be identified early, allowing the project management 
 team to take proactive measures to stay on track. 
 Use Case 
 Let's consider 
 ABC Developers, a real estate development company working on a new luxury 
 apartment complex called Sky Project. They use an ERP software, designed 
 specifically for real estate to manage their projects. Within this system, 
 they create a detailed schedule outlining all key milestones for the Skyline 
 Residences project.

 by ABC Developers

 the respective apartment.

 for the respective apartment.

 Tutorial: Creating 
 Plan Revenue Heads 
 Plan Revenue 
 Heads 
 Plan Revenue Heads refers to the process of defining, categorising, 
 and organising various sources of revenue that a real estate company expects 
 to generate. These revenue heads may include sales of properties, property 
 management fees, etc. 
 What is the Need for Planning Revenue Heads? 
 Improved Financial Management : 
 By clearly defining revenue streams, the company can track and monitor 
 their financial performance more effectively. This can help in identifying 
 profitable revenue sources and areas that may need improvement. 
 Accurate Budgeting and Forecasting : 
 Planning revenue heads allows the company to create more accurate 
 budgets and forecasts. By having a clear picture of expected revenue 
 from each source, the company can set realistic financial goals and 
 make informed decisions. 
 Enhanced Reporting : Properly 
 planned revenue heads facilitate better reporting capabilities within 
 the software. The company can generate detailed financial reports 
 showing revenue breakdowns by source, which can be useful for internal 
 analysis as well as for external stakeholders. 
 Resource Allocation : With a clear 
 understanding of revenue heads, the company can allocate resources 
 more effectively. They can focus their efforts on revenue streams 
 that are more profitable and make adjustments where needed. 
 Compliance and Taxation : Properly 
 planned revenue heads can help ensure compliance with financial regulations 
 and accurate reporting for tax purposes. By categorising revenue correctly, 
 the company can minimise the risk of errors and penalties. 
 Use Case Example 
 A real estate company took up a residential 
 property development project. They implement the payment structure within 
 the software under the specific revenue head. Each residential unit comes 
 as a fixed price. 
 Upon securing a buyer for a unit, the 
 buyer pays the initial booking amount of 10% to reserve the property. 
 As the project progresses, the buyer makes subsequent payments based on 
 specific milestones achieved in the construction process. 
 The buyer / property owner pays 10% 
 of the unit cost upon completion of foundation work. 
 Another 60% is paid upon the completion 
 of the specific floor in the building. 
 Subsequently, 10% is paid upon the completion 
 of interior finishing. 
 Finally, the remaining 10% is paid upon 
 the handover of the property to the buyer. 
 Project wise Payment Plan Schedule or Milestone 
 is required to be tagged against the Revenue heads here. Schedule 
 wise Revenue head wise percentage or amount to be defined in the detail 
 grid.

 Select the Payment Plan

 Business

 name the Business Unit will be auto populated 
 Project

 selection of Payment Plan name the Project Hierarchy will be auto populated

 wise percentage or Amount 
 Click 'Save'

 To search the data user can use the normal search or can use the advance 
 search interface 
 Tutorial: Creating Plan Revenue Heads

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Reversal Reason
text:
Reversal Reason 
 Help > Setup > Revenue Head or Scheme" />
 Reversal 
 Reason 
 A Reversal Reason in the context of a receipt 
 refers to the explanation or justification behind reversing a previously 
 recorded receipt transaction. When a receipt reversal occurs, it means 
 that a payment previously received and recorded is being canceled or reversed 
 for a specific reason. This action could be due to various factors such 
 as dishonoured cheques, cancellation of services, or errors in payment 
 processing. 
 Use Case 
 Scenario: A property owner had initially 
 provided a cheque of Rs. 2,00,000 as a payment for his property. However, 
 the cheque was dishonoured by the bank due to insufficient funds in the 
 owner’s account. 
 Reversal Reason 
 The Reversal Reason in this scenario 
 could be attributed to the dishonoured cheque from the property owner, 
 indicating that the initial payment of Rs. 2,00,000 was cancelled due 
 to non-sufficient funds, and the receipt needed to be reversed accordingly. 
 By providing clear and specific 
 reversal reasons for this scenario, the developer can maintain accurate 
 and financial records, ensuring transparency and accountability in their 
 operations. 
 Steps To Setup Reversal Reason 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Setup> Revenue Head / Scheme> Reversal Reason. The 
 following window will appear. 
 1 . 2. Fill in 
 the Code and Description. 
 The Code being a short form of the Reversal 
 Reason and the Description being the actual 
 reason itself. Once done, click on Submit. 
 1. 3. V iew the 
 entry by clicking on the Advanced Search icon on top-right corner of the 
 screen. The entries can be viewed as follows. 
 1. 4. Now, navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Collection> Receipt. This screen should be visible. Choose 
 the Business Unit after which the Reason field will unlock. 
 There will be a drop-down list there from where the required reason is 
 chosen. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 Revenue 
 Head 
 Revenue 
 heads refer to various 
 streams of income that a developer can generate from a property. These 
 include unit cost, maintenance charges, and other related parameters where 
 customers pay the developer for services provided. Properly planning and 
 managing these revenue heads is crucial for the financial health and sustainability 
 of real estate projects. 
 Key Revenue Heads in Real 
 Estate 
 1. Unit 
 Cost: This 
 is the primary source of revenue for developers. It includes the price 
 paid by buyers for purchasing a unit in the development, whether it's 
 a residential apartment, commercial space, or any other type of property. 
 The unit cost is determined based on factors like location, amenities, 
 market demand, and construction quality. 
 2. Maintenance 
 Charges: Maintenance 
 charges are fees collected from property owners to cover the upkeep of 
 common areas, facilities, and services. This includes landscaping, cleaning, 
 security, repairs, and utilities for common spaces. Regular collection 
 of maintenance charges ensures the property remains in good condition 
 and services are consistently provided. 
 3. Parking 
 Fees: In 
 many real estate developments, especially in urban areas, parking spaces 
 are limited and valuable. Developers can charge for parking spots, either 
 as a one-time purchase or as a monthly rental fee. This provides an additional 
 revenue stream and helps manage the allocation of parking spaces. 
 4. Amenities 
 Fees: Developers 
 often include various amenities like gyms, swimming pools, clubhouses, 
 and recreational areas in their projects. Access to these amenities can 
 be monetised through membership fees or usage charges. This not only generates 
 extra income but also enhances the attractiveness of the property. 
 5. Utility 
 Fees: Utility 
 fees cover the cost of providing essential services like water, electricity, 
 gas, and internet. These are either included in the maintenance charges 
 or billed separately based on usage. Properly managing utility fees ensures 
 that the costs are fairly distributed among the residents. 
 All 
 types of costs to be received from customers are defined as revenue heads 
 and to be created here. Examples of revenue heads may include Unit Cost, 
 Land Cost, Vehicle Parking, Extra Charges Normal, Extra Charges Income, 
 Late Payment Charges, Floor Rise Charges, Cancellation Charges, etc.

 Late Payment Fee refers to the additional charge imposed on property 
 buyers/owners who fail to make timely payments for the purchase of properties. 
 These fees are typically included in the terms of the purchase agreement 
 and are intended to encourage timely payments and compensate for the costs 
 incurred by the builder due to delayed payments. 
 This is applicable in the following 
 scenario: 
 Scenario 
 Consistent Delayed Payments : 
 Buyers who consistently delay their payments beyond the agreed-upon due 
 dates may be subject to additional late payment fees. This serves as a 
 deterrent to discourage habitual late payments and enforce adherence to 
 payment schedules.

title: Reminder Setup
text:
Reminder Setup 
 Help > Setup > Demand or Reminder or LPF" />
 Reminder 
 Setup 
 Age Wise Reminder Setup 
 This 
 section provides the steps required to follow up with the property buyers 
 / owners for their outstanding dues. 
 This setup is based on the age of the 
 outstanding invoices. 
 The user (typically the accounts receivable 
 or collection team) sets up a timeline or schedule for sending reminders. 
 Let’s take an example where the system 
 is configured to send a first reminder after 15 days of the invoice due 
 date, a second reminder after 30 days of the invoice dua date, and a final 
 reminder after 60 days post the invoice due date. 
 The purpose is to automate the collection 
 process and ensure that customers are consistently reminded about their 
 outstanding payments. 
 With this, a large volume of invoices 
 can be streamlined on their collection efforts. 
 Steps to Setup Reminder (Age-wise) 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Setup> Demand / Reminder / LPF> Reminder Setup. 
 2. 2. 
 This window will be visible. 
 3. Fill in the fields: Business Unit, Reminder 
 Basis, Effected Date. Upon selecting the preferred Business Unit, 
 move towards Reminder Basis tab. From the dropdown list, choose 
 the option Reminder AgeWise. Insert the Effected Date from 
 which this reminder would be applicable. 
 4. Click 
 on Add New Row from where the Reminder Header window will 
 open. 
 5. Fill 
 in the fields accordingly. These include Value Type, Operator, Minimum 
 Value/ Minimum Percentage, Reminder Days, Report Format, Email Format, 
 and SMS Format. 
 Under Value Type, two options 
 are available: 
 Percentage Based: Choose this option if the reminder is going to be 
 sent based on a specific percentage of the due amount. 
 Lumpsum / Fixed: Choose this option if the reminder is going to be 
 sent based on a lumpsum amount of the outstanding due. 
 Use Case: If you choose the Value Type as Percentage 
 Based, the Minimum Value field would become inactive. If the 
 Value Type is chosen as Lumpsum / Fixed, the Minimum 
 Percentage field would become inactive. 
 Under Operator, there is only 
 one parameter available which is: > (greater than). This denotes the 
 criteria where the reminder would only be generated when the due amount 
 is greater than the set values in the Minimum Value / Minimum Percentage. 
 Under the Reminder Days field, 
 insert the number of days after which the reminder would be sent at intervals 
 like 15 days, 30 days, and 60 days after the invoice due date, respectively. 
 Choose 
 the Report 
 Format (report sent as an attachment to the property owner), SMS Format (required SMS template ), and Email Format 
 ( required e-mail template), as applicable. 
 6. After all the details are filled in, click on Save. 
 P.S: Likewise, three entries are made against 
 this Reminder Setup- for 15, 30 & 60 days respectively. 
 7. Once saved, the following 
 grid will appear where the Reminders can be 
 seen. Click on Submit 
 once done. 
 8. Next, click on the advanced search icon on 
 the top-right corner of the screen. The new Reminder would be displayed 
 as follows. 
 P.S: There is an option available where the 
 scheduler can be set to generate and send this Reminder to the respective 
 Property Owners. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 Mapping 
 Bank Mapping helps in organising and categorising financial information 
 related to customer accounts. 
 What is Bank Mapping? 
 Bank 
 Mapping involves associating 
 a particular project with its corresponding bank accounts. This association 
 facilitates the tracking of customer payments. Failure to do so when creating 
 a Receipt could lead to user 
 confusion regarding the selection of the appropriate bank account for 
 the project, potentially resulting in an incorrect transaction. 
 Use Case 
 A real estate company can use bank mapping 
 to link each business unit / project to the respective bank accounts. 
 When a customer makes a payment for purchasing a property, the system 
 can update the transaction details and link them to the project’s bank 
 account. This ensures accurate tracking of payments and seamless reconciliation 
 with the company’s financial records. 
 Steps to Setup Bank Mapping 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Setup> Account Integration> Bank Mapping. This screen 
 should be visible. 
 1 . 2. 
 Fill in the field: Business Unit, 
 Allotted To, and Select Bank. Choose the Business Unit 
 from the drop-down list. After that, the Allotted To drop-down 
 list will show the developer’s name from where the necessary selected 
 needs to be made. Choose the bank name under Select Bank field. 
 The bank details will be auto populated. Your screen will look like this. 
 Once done click on Submit. 
 1 . 3.

 shown as follows.

 Block Unit 
 Use Case 
 In a real estate 
 development project, a customer expresses interest in a specific unit

 the booking amount. The developer logs into the CRM portal, navigates 
 to the project's unit management section, and selects the desired unit. 
 Using the CRM's block feature, the developer marks the unit as "Blocked" 
 or "Hold," entering the customer's details and the hold duration. 
 The CRM system confirms the unit is blocked and updates its status. The 
 CRM system monitors the hold period, ensuring the unit remains blocked. 
 P.S: If the 
 "Blocked Until" date has passed, the unit will be shown as available 
 to all users. 
 This interface 
 is used if it is required to block a particular unit (Flat, Shop etc.)

title: Booking Amendment
text:
Booking Amendment 
 Help > Transaction > Booking" />
 Tutorial: Creating Booking Amendment 
 Booking 
 Amendment 
 After initial 
 booking, changes may be required in terms of area, charge, unit, name 
 etc. This interface is used for such amendments or changes in booking. 
 Business 
 Unit : Select the concerned business unit 
 Financial 
 Year : It gets populated, however user 
 can select another as per requirement 
 Document Type : 
 It gets populated, however user can select another as per requirement 
 Booking 
 Amendment 
 Document Date : 
 It shows as on date by default. User can set another date. 
 Document No : 
 It is generated after the entry saved 
 Booking 
 No : Select the booking number. (Data comes from Transaction > 
 Booking > Booking ) 
 Project 
 Hierarchy : project hierarchy gets populated after selection of 
 booking number 
 Unit 
 No : Unit number gets populated after selection of booking number 
 Applicant : 
 The name of the applicant gets populated after selection of booking number 
 Clicking 
 on the required revenue head, the cost details of the selected revenue 
 head will open. For example, in the above screen user clicks on 'Unit 
 Cost' row. The cost details section of the unit cost will open as shown 
 in the picture below. 
 Click on 
 the required schedule to edit. The 'Edit_Schedule' popup box will open. 
 Here amount can be edited and saved. 
 Once the 
 Booking Amendment entry got finally approved then only the “Is Amended” 
 flag will be updated as YES in Booking Header. 
 The 
 Booking amendment entry must be saved in provisional mode. 
 Different 
 Document Types 
 ( View the reports of these amendments ) 
 Booking Amendment 
 Area Change 
 Charge Change 
 Name Change 
 Buyer Change 
 Booking Cancel 
 Unit Change 
 Area Change 
 To change the area it is required 
 to select 'Area Change' as document type 
 Click on 
 the row under 'Area Info' to edit the area 
 Enter the 
 changed area in New_Area field and click 'Save' 
 Click on 
 the row in 'Cost Detail' section to edit schedule 
 Tutorial: Creating 
 Booking Amendment Area Change 
 Charge Change 
 To change the charge it is required 
 to select 'Charge Change' as document type 
 Click on 
 the row under 'Rate Info' to edit the rate 
 Click on 
 the row in 'Cost Detail' section to edit schedule 
 Tutorial: Creating 
 Booking Amendment Charge Change 
 Name Change 
 To change the name it is required 
 to select 'Name Change' as document type. 
 Select 
 the booking number. Applicant and existing co-applicants details will 
 populate in the grid. Select the co-applicants one by one and select display 
 sequence numbers from 1-10 as per the requirement. 
 In case of 
 adding a new co-applicant, click on "ADD New Row". Fill the 
 applicant details manually or click on "Existing" checkbox to 
 add an existing applicant. Select 
 the display sequence numbers from 1-10 as per the requirement. 
 Add 
 new applicant's name. 
 Select the 
 old applicant name and click on 'Remove Row' 
 Notes: 
 In 
 case of Primary Applicant Name change, the Primary Applicant Name and 
 the Finance Ledger Description will be updated on the final approval of 
 the Name Change entry. 
 Now 
 system will update the Primary Applicant Name and the Finance Ledger Description 
 on the final approval of the Name Change entry in case of Primary Applicant 
 Name change. 
 Once 
 the Name change entry got finally approved then only the Primary Applicant 
 Name and the Finance Ledger Description will be updated in Booking Header 
 and in Finance Account Head master respectively. 
 The Booking amendment entry (Name Change) must be 
 saved in provisional mode. 
 Tutorial: Creating 
 Booking Amendment Name Change 
 Buyer Change 
 Once 
 the Buyer change entry got finally approved then only the New Primary 
 Applicant’s Name, New Application number, and the Finance Ledger Description 
 will be updated in Booking Header and in Finance Account Head master respectively. 
 The Booking amendment entry 
 (Buyer Change) must be saved in provisional mode. 
 Notes: 
 1. In case the Business Unit is having 
 NET Posting methodology then Buyer Change entry will not be allowed 
 Now system 
 will not allow making Buyer Change entry against the Booking if the that 
 booking is belongs to the Business Unit which is having NET posting methodology. 
 Step1: 
 Select the business unit which is having NET Posting methodology 
 Step2: 
 Select financial Year, select Document Type as Buyer Change, select document 
 date, and select the respective customer name 
 Step3: 
 Select the “To Application Number” 
 Step4: 
 Now click on SUBMIT button and check that system is not allowing to save 
 the Buyer Change entry as this Business Unit is having NET posting methodology 
 2. System will restrict to deletion of any Buyer 
 Transfer entry from Pending Approval 
 Step 1: Make one Buyer Transfer entry 
 Step 2: Log in with the approver’s login credential 
 Step 3: Now go to Pending Approval screen 
 Step 4: Now select the Buyer Transfer document 
 Step 5: Now click on Continue and then click 
 on Delete Document option 
 Step 
 6: Now click on Submit 
 Step 
 7: Now check that system shows a Validation message and not allowing to 
 delete the Buyer 
 Transfer entry 
 Booking Cancel 
 To cancel the booking it is 
 required to select 'Booking Cancel' as document type 
 In case of Booking Cancellation 
 entry, “Is cancelled” flag will be updated in Booking Header, application 
 cancelled flag and application. 
 cancelled 
 date will be updated in application details header on final approval of 
 the Booking Cancellation entry. 
 The 
 Finance Ledger Description will also be updated with the text as "cancelled" 
 on final approval of the Booking Cancellation entry. 
 Now 
 system will update the “Is cancelled” flag in Booking Header, application 
 cancelled flag and application cancelled date in application details header 
 on final approval of the Booking Cancellation entry. 
 The 
 Finance Ledger Description will also be updated with the text as "cancelled" 
 on final approval of the Booking Cancellation entry. 
 Once the Booking Cancellation entry got finally approved 
 then only the “Is cancelled” flag will be updated in Booking Header, application 
 cancelled flag and application cancelled date will be updated in application 
 details header. 
 The Finance Ledger Description will also be updated 
 with the text as "cancelled" on final approval of the Booking 
 Cancellation entry. 
 Note: 
 The Remark field can be set as a mandatory field through Metadata. 
 Select the Reason 
 created in Reason 
 Master (Formula Based) against the Entry Type Booking Amendment 
 and Document Type Booking Cancel. 
 Select the appropriate Reason and confirm that the 
 system auto-populates/calculates the Cancellation Charge Amount based 
 on the selected Reason. 
 Users will be able to see the 
 “Brokerage Details” while making Booking Cancellation entry without tagging 
 Note for Approval document. 
 Step 1: Go to Booking > 
 Booking Amendment 
 Step 2: Select Business Unit, Financial Year, Document 
 Date, Document Type as Booking Cancel, Customer Name. 
 Step 3: Now clicks on the “Detail” button and check. 
 Step 4: Here user will be able to view the “Outstanding 
 Amount”, “LPF Amount”, “Total Amount of Outstanding and LPF Amount”, “Broker 
 Name”, “Brokerage”, “Brokerage Bill Amount (Basic)”, “Non Reversible Tax” 
 and “Loan Bank Name”. 
 Step 5: Now check that Broker Name, Brokerage amount, 
 Brokerage Bill Amount (Basic) is showing under the Brokerage Details heading. 
 The Booking amendment entry (Booking Cancel) must 
 be saved in provisional mode. 
 Unit Change 
 Now 
 system will update the New Primary Unit No, New Primary Unit’s Project 
 Hierarchy in Booking Header and the Finance Ledger Description in Finance 
 Account Head on the final approval of the Unit Change entry. 
 Once 
 the Unit Change entry got finally approved then only the New Primary Unit 
 No., New Primary Unit’s Project Hierarchy and the Finance Ledger Description 
 will be updated in Booking Header and in Finance Account Head master respectively. 
 Before Approval 
 After Approval 
 The Booking amendment entry (Unit Change) must be 
 saved in provisional mode. 
 Notes: 
 1. 
 Users will be able to use the button while making 
 Booking Cancellation entry without tagging Note 
 for Approval document. 
 Here user will be able to view 
 the “Outstanding Amount”, “LPF Amount”, “Total Amount of Outstanding and 
 LPF Amount”, “Brokerage Amount”, “Non Reversible Tax” and “Loan Bank Name”. 
 2. 
 A new validation has been incorporated in Booking Cancel entry, if BRS 
 against the Bank Receipts are not done then system will not allow saving 
 the Booking Cancel entry. 
 Now 
 system will validate the BRS against Bank Receipt while making Booking 
 Cancel entry through Booking Amendment. 
 Step 1 : Select Business Unit, Financial 
 Year, Document Type-Booking Cancel, and Document Date. Select a Customer 
 Name who is having few bank receipts without BRS. 
 Step 2 : Now go to the Credit Note 
 Tab and select all the invoices for Auto Credit Note entry. 
 Step 3 : Now click on Submit 
 Step 4 : Now check that system is 
 not allowing to save this Booking Cancel entry and showing a validation 
 message as “Booking Cancellation entry cannot be saved as BRS not found 
 against some of receipts” 
 3. Attachment Delete 
 option in Booking Amendment 
 Users 
 will be able to delete attachment in Booking Amendment entry 
 Step1: 
 Find any booking amendment entry which is having Attachment 
 Step2: 
 Click on Delete Attachment, the attachment popup will open 
 Step3: 
 Select the attachment which is required to delete and then just click 
 on 'Remove Row' as shown below 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 Info

 Hierarchy : Select project hierarchy

 and save the booking entry. 
 Create/Edit Agreement, Permission to Mortgage

 icon.

text:

 Offer of 
 Possession 
 Offer of

 all dues which had to be paid and receipt of payment details against them. 
 Stamp Duty, legal fees have to be paid but they were not part of the agreement, 
 are a payment for a service not being provided by the developer. 
 This is a memorandum entry, there is no impact 
 on financial ledgers, no link with invoice/money receipt. 
 It will not give any financial effect in Finance 
 module. It is only for information purpose.

title: Proforma Invoice
text:
Proforma Invoice 
 Help > Transaction > Proforma Invoice" />
 Proforma 
 Invoice 
 Proforma Invoice (PI) can be used to provide 
 a request for payment against an upcoming demand. Proforma Invoice has 
 no financial or statutory Impact. This is mainly used to intimate customers 
 for payable amount, and to raise invoice after receipt of payment so that 
 tax liability is not created beforehand. 
 Outstanding payment details are available against 
 Proforma Invoices through Order-wise Outstanding report. Reminders for 
 payments against PI are in the product roadmap and will be available after 
 some time.

title: Credit Note
text:
Credit Note 
 Help > Transaction > Invoicing" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Credit Note 
 Credit Note 
 Credit Note 
 is a brief written document (Note) produced to reduce/adjust the amount 
 of payable. It shows the details of refund due to a customer. Under normal 
 conditions, Credit Note presents the equivalent details of an invoice. 
 When users 
 raise invoices to the customers then they debit their account. On certain 
 occasions, 
 they credit their account by issuing a Credit Note.

 Business Unit : 
 Select business unit 
 Financial Year : 
 It gets populated, however user can select another as per requirement 
 Document Type : 
 It gets populated, however user can select another as per requirement

 It shows as on date by default. User can set another date. 
 Document No : 
 It is generated after the entry saved

 Select customer (Data comes from Transaction 
 > Booking > Customer Details )

 Booking number gets populated (Data comes from Transaction 
 > Booking > Booking )

 comes from Setup 
 > Unit > Unit )

 Select Goods and Services Tax Identification Number for registered supplier, 
 for unregistered supplier select Unregistered >> State Name

 of Supply :

 Tutorial: 
 Creating Credit Note 
 View reports of Credit Note 
 Demand Reversal 
 Demand 
 reversal refers to the situation where a previously made demand is reversed 
 or cancelled. This can happen for various reasons such as errors in invoicing, 
 disputes with customers or changes in agreements. This is done via Credit 
 Note and a new invoice may be generated for the correct amount or with 
 the necessary changes. Demand reversal is a common practice in business 
 transactions to rectify mistakes and ensure accurate financial records. 
 This 
 can occur in two primary scenarios: 
 Scenario 
 1: If 
 a demand (invoice) is mistakenly raised against a customer, a demand reversal 
 entry is made to cancel that demand. This allows for the same demand to 
 be raised against the same schedule/milestone in the future when it is 
 appropriate. 
 Scenario 
 2: Another 
 example of demand reversal occurs when a customer requests an extension 
 of the payment date. By reversing the demand, the payment date can be 
 extended, addressing the customer’s request. 
 Steps to Perform Demand 
 Reversal 
 1. 1. Navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Invoicing> Credit Note. The following screen can be seen. 
 Choose the appropriate Business Unit and enter the document date 
 as per the demand reversal / credit note date. Select the relevant Customer 
 from the list. Once the Customer is selected, the following grid 
 will display all schedule-wise revenue heads. 
 2. 2.Select the specific Schedule/Revenue 
 head as needed. 
 3. 3. The following window will open. 
 Mark the ‘ Demand Reversal’ option and proceed by clicking on the 
 Next button. 
 4. 4.T he billing term will be automatically 
 calculated at this stage. Click on Finish. The following screen 
 would appear. 
 5. 5. Click on Process Data after 
 the changes have been made so that the Ledger posting is complete. Now 
 click on Submit to proceed further. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

text:
Payment to Customer 
 Help > Transaction > Collection" />
 Payment 
 to Customer 
 This 
 Interface is used for making payment to 
 a customer. Payment to customer can be required in case of to be done 
 cancellation of unit, return of excess payment received. Any payment that 
 needs to be paid can be done against On Account amount available. Refundable 
 amount is the maximum amount which can be refunded. Refund amount is the 
 amount which is being refunded through a Payment to Customer transaction 
 entry. 
 After 
 saving this form, Cheque can be printed from Finance > Transaction 
 > Banking > Cheque Printing . 
 Accounts 
 heads are debited and credited based on this transaction. Even though 
 there will be no separate voucher in Finance module, account head posting 
 is done from here. It will reflect in respective ledger heads. 
 Business 
 Unit : Select business unit 
 Financial 
 Year : It gets populated, however 
 user can select another as per requirement 
 Document Type : Default document 
 type for this form is Payment to Customer Real Estate or any other doc 
 type linked to this type of entry. Doc type is defined through 
 Administration

title: Bulk Additional Brokerage
text:
Bulk Additional Brokerage 
 Help > Transaction > Brokerage" />
 Bulk 
 Additional Brokerage 
 Broker refers to a firm or individual broker who 
 facilitates transactions between buyers and sellers of properties. Properties 
 include residential homes, commercial buildings, or land. These brokers 
 are intermediaries, utilizing their market knowledge and negotiation skills 
 to ensure successful and smooth transactions between parties. Usually, 
 there’s a fixed brokerage fee, typically a percentage of a property’s 
 sale price, or according to the pre-set brokerage ladder for their services. 
 Additional (add-on) brokerage 
 is an ad-hoc/lumpsum fee that comes 
 into play for exceptional services or value-added assistance provided 
 beyond the standard duties of a real estate broker. 
 Let’s discuss a few scenarios where 
 “additional brokerage” is given based on the following parameters: 
 Scenario 1 
 Large Transaction Volume : A broker 
 may receive additional brokerage for handling a high volume of transactions 
 or for exceeding a specific target set by the brokerage firm or client. 
 Scenario 2 
 Exceptional Performance to Meet Specific 
 Targets : Brokers who demonstrate exceptional performance, such as 
 consistently achieving high sales, providing outstanding customer service, 
 or acquiring a particular number of new accounts, may be rewarded with 
 additional brokerage as an incentive. This serves as a motivation and 
 reward for successful outcomes. 
 Scenario 3 
 Complex Transactions : Brokers 
 who successfully handle complex transactions, such as mergers and acquisitions, 
 may receive additional compensation for their expertise and specialized 
 skills. 
 P.S.: It is important to note that the 
 provision of additional brokerage to brokers is subject to the policies 
 and regulations of the firm, as well as any relevant standards and legal 
 requirements. 
 Steps to Perform Bulk Additional Brokerage 
 for a Single Broker 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and Customer Care> 
 Brokerage> Bulk Additional Brokerage 
 1. 2. Insert 
 the details marked in red. These include Broker, Amount, and Description. 
 1 . 3. 
 Click on Next to reach the 
 Output tab. Select the Units for which the broker will be provided 
 the Additional Brokerage. 
 1. 4. 
 Click on Generate to proceed 
 further. 
 The preferred broker will 
 get the “Additional Brokerage” distributed against multiple properties 
 or as agreed with the broker.

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Bill Inward
text:
Bill Inward 
 Help > Transaction > Brokerage" />
 Bill 
 Inward 
 Bill 
 Inward refers to the process 
 of acknowledging and recording a bill received from a vendor within the 
 system to ensure that it is accounted for and not misplaced. It involves 
 verifying the details of the bill, confirming its receipt, and processing 
 it for further action, such as payment or approval. 
 Benefits 
 of Creating a Bill Inward 
 Efficiency: 
 The process streamlines the bill processing 
 for workflow, reducing manual errors and saving time in handling bills. 
 Transparency: 
 It provides visibility into the status 
 of bills, ensuring that they are acknowledged and accounted for promptly. 
 Compliance: 
 It helps to maintain accurate financial 
 records and ensure that they are acknowledged and accounted for promptly. 
 Supplier 
 Relationships: It can improve 
 relationships with suppliers by ensuring timely acknowledgement and processing 
 of bills, leading to smoother transactions. 
 Use Case 
 Brokers 
 are constantly dealing with a high volume of financial transactions and 
 invoices related to trades, commissions, and fees. Implementing an efficient 
 bill inward system can be highly beneficial in streamlining the billing 
 process and improving overall efficiency. 
 When 
 a broker completes a trade or earns a commission, the correspondence invoice 
 is generated. Without a dedicated bill inward process, there is a risk 
 of invoices being overlooked, misplaced, or not processed in a timely 
 manner, leading to delays in commission payouts and potential discrepancies 
 in financial records. 
 As 
 soon as the invoice gets generated for a broker, it is promptly acknowledged 
 within the system. The details of the invoice are verified, and the necessary 
 approvals are obtained for payment processing. This ensures that brokers 
 receive their commissions accurately and on time, leading to improved 
 satisfaction and trust among each other. 
 Steps 
 to Perform Bill Inward for Brokerage 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Brokerage> Bill Inward. The following screen would be 
 visible. 
 1. 2. 
 Insert data to the respective fields 
 such as: Business

 Head, Party Bill No, Party Bill Date, and Remarks

title: Bulk Retrospective Brokerage
text:
Bulk Retrospective Brokerage 
 Help > Transaction > Brokerage" />
 Bulk Retrospective 
 Brokerage 
 Bulk Retrospective Brokerage 
 refers to the process of calculating 
 and releasing commissions (brokerage) for brokers based on multiple bookings 
 or transactions after those transactions have occurred. This approach 
 allows for an efficient aggregation and processing of brokerage entitlements 
 for multiple bookings in one go, rather than processing each one individually. 
 Why is Bulk Retrospective Brokerage Beneficial? 
 The key benefit of Bulk Retrospective 
 Brokerage with automatic adjustment based on set slab rates is increased 
 efficiency and accuracy in brokerage calculations. 
 Automatic adjustment based on slab rates 
 ensures that brokerage fees are calculated consistently and in line with 
 the agreed-upon rates. 
 Use Case 
 Consider a real estate firm that has 
 several property bookings managed by the same broker. Here is the scenario: 
 1. 1 . Bookings Assigned: 
 The broker manages four property bookings, 
 all of which have been tagged with the same brokerage template. 
 2. 2. Initial Brokerage Release: 
 For the first two bookings, the broker 
 is set to receive a brokerage of 3%. 
 3. 3. Bulk Retrospective Entry: 
 Instead of calculating and releasing 
 the brokerage for each booking individually, the firm processes a bulk 
 retrospective brokerage entry. This includes all four bookings, applying 
 the 3% brokerage rate consistently. 
 4. 4. Adjustments and New Rates: 
 Later, a fifth booking is entered 
 for a different project but managed by the same broker. This booking qualifies 
 for a new brokerage rate of 4%. 
 5. 5. Updated Processing: The retrospective brokerage process 
 is updated to accommodate the new booking and the increased brokerage 
 rate, ensuring that the broker receives the correct commission for all 
 transactions efficiently. 
 Steps to Perform 
 Bulk Retrospective Brokerage 
 1. 1. 
 Creating 
 the Brokerage Template 
 Basis Selection: Choose ‘Slab’ as the basis. 
 Unit Basis: Set the slab to ‘Units’. 
 Calculation Basis: Select ‘Percentage Based’. 
 Calculation Formula: Provide the necessary calculation formula. 
 2. 
 Brokerage Release 
 · Users can create a brokerage release plan as required. 
 3 . 
 3.Enter two bookings with the same broker, brokerage template, and release 
 template. 
 4. Raise invoices against the two bookings. 
 5. Confirm receipt of payment for both 
 bookings. 
 6. Based on the brokerage template, 
 release brokerage fees. 
 7.Now enter the third and fourth bookings 
 tagged with the same broker, broker template, and release template 
 8. After the brokerage template setup, 
 the broker is eligible for 3% brokerage for all bookings. 
 9. 
 To release 3% brokerage for all the bookings, the user needs to pass a 
 bulk retrospective brokerage entry 
 10. After generating the retrospective brokerage 
 process, book the Broker Invoice where all four bookings’ brokerage is 
 shown. 
 11. Enter the fifth booking in Another 
 Project Reserver tagging with the same broker and the same template. 
 12. After entering the fifth booking, the same 
 broker is now eligible for 4% brokerage. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Brokerage Modification / Salesperson Modification
text:
Brokerage / Salesperson Modification 
 Help > Transaction > Brokerage" />
 Brokerage 
 / Salesperson Modification 
 This model refers to a process that allows updating 
 or modifying brokerages/brokers /salesperson assigned to specific bookings. 
 It is handy when there is a need to change or update the brokerage or 
 salesperson associated with a particular booking due to various reasons 
 such as performance, restructuring, or changes in business relationships. 
 What is the Need for Brokerage / Salesperson Modification? 
 The main benefit of this feature is 
 the flexibility it provides in managing brokerages and salespersons within 
 different business units. It allows businesses to adapt to changing circumstances, 
 improve efficiency, and ensure that the right resources are allocated 
 where they are most needed. By enabling easy modifications to brokerages 
 and salespersons, businesses can optimise their operations, improve client 
 satisfaction, and ultimately drive better results. 
 Use Case 
 Consider a real estate developer with 
 multiple business units, each with different brokers/salesperson handling 
 property sales. If a broker/salesperson needs to be moved from one business 
 unit to another, there’s this model that makes this transition smooth 
 and efficient. 
 Brokerages: The system lets the user update the brokerage details 
 quickly, making sure the brokerage aligns with the new business unit. 
 Brokers: Reassigning 
 brokers from one unit to another is straightforward, with the system updating 
 their information to reflect their new assignment. 
 Salespersons: Any adjustments to modify/update the salesperson 
 can be easily managed, ensuring everyone is correctly aligned with the 
 right business unit. 
 Steps to Perform Brokerage/Salesperson Modification 
 Benefit of Updating/Modifying Broker/Brokerage 
 When managing 
 multiple business units and brokers, it's essential to ensure that the 
 correct broker and brokerage details are recorded accurately. Here is 
 a quick guide on how to update or modify broker/brokerage information, 
 especially when users might forget to input these details during booking. 
 1. 1. Navigate to Sales and Customer Care> 
 Brokerage> Brokerage/Salesperson Modification. This screen will 
 be visible. Enter the Business Unit and Booking No. 
 1. 2. 
 Click on the Edit option on 
 the top of the window upon which the Broker Type field will unlock. 
 1. 3. 
 From the drop-down list, choose either of the two options. 
 Sharing Multiple : 
 This refers to a situation where multiple brokers are involved in a single 
 transaction or deal. This means that the commission or fees earned from 
 the transaction are distributed among multiple brokers who were part of 
 the deal. Sharing multiple is common in situations where different brokers 
 bring in different clients, expertise, or resources to complete a transaction 
 collaboratively. 
 Non-Sharing 
 Single/Multiple : This refers to a situation where a single broker 
 handles a transaction exclusively without sharing commission with other 
 brokers. 
 Now, let’s 
 discuss Non-Sharing Single/Multiple which is the most common forms 
 of brokerage. 
 4. Choose the 
 option which says Non-Sharing Single/Multiple upon which the following 
 window will open. Now, click on add new row to update/modify the 
 entry. 
 5.The following 
 screen will appear where the respective entries must be made, such as: 
 Broker Name, Brokerage Template, Brokerage Release, MOU No. (auto-populated), 
 and MOU Date (auto-populated). These are all the mandatory fields. 
 6. Once the 
 Broker Name is selected for a particular Business Unit, the screen 
 would look similar to the following. Please see that the AssessableAmt, 
 Brokerage %, BrokerageAmt, and Net Amt. i s automatically generated. 
 This data is pulled from the respective template. 
 7. After clicking 
 on Save, the data can be seen in the grid as follows. Click on 
 Submit to save the entry. 
 Now, 
 if we were to discuss the Non-Sharing Single/Multiple broker type, 
 the steps would be very similar to what we discussed previously. The only 
 difference would be, after selecting the Add New Row the following 
 screen would appear. 
 1. 1. Enter the Broker Name, Brokerage 
 Template, Brokerage Release (mandatory fields). Check the Is Primary option to choose the broker selected 
 as primary. Enter the Sharing 
 %. Click on Save 
 once the entries have been made. 
 P.S: Please note that the brokerage 
 sharing percentage must always total 100%. It cannot exceed or fall short 
 of this amount to ensure accurate and fair distribution. 
 2.The following grid will show the entry. 
 Click on Submit to save the entry. 
 3.Now, 
 proceed with repeating the same steps above to make another entry. After 
 making the second entry, the following grid would be visible. Click on 
 Submit once done. 
 Now 
 moving on to updating the Salesperson /CRO /Payment for a specific booking. 
 Benefit of Updating/Modifying Salesperson/CRO/Payment 
 Plan 
 When managing 
 salesperson/CRO/payment plan, it's crucial to ensure that all salesperson, 
 CRO, and payment plan details are accurately recorded. Here is a quick 
 guide on how to update or modify these details, especially when users might forget 
 to input these details during booking. 
 1. 1. 
 On the top of the screen, there is 
 an option Salesperson/CRO/Payment Plan. Click on that upon which 
 the following screen will open. Choose the Business Unit and Booking 
 No. 
 1. 2. 
 Click on Edit. Now the option to tag Salesperson, CRO, and 
 Plan Name will unlock. 
 1 . Tag the respective Salesperson , 
 CRO , 
 and choose the Plan 
 Name applicable. Once done, click on Submit and the following screen 
 will appear. 
 P.S. When updating the Plan Name , 
 please note that at this change applies only to the ‘ name’ itself 
 and does not affect any integrations within the Plan. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 commercial buildings, or land. These brokers are intermediaries, utilizing 
 their market knowledge and negotiation skills to ensure successful and 
 smooth transactions between parties. Usually, there’s a fixed brokerage 
 fee, typically a percentage of a property’s sale price, or according to 
 the pre-set brokerage ladder for their services. 
 Additional (add-on) brokerage 
 is an ad-hoc/lumpsum fee that comes 
 into play for exceptional services or value-added assistance provided 
 beyond the standard duties of a real estate broker. 
 Let’s discuss a few scenarios where 
 “additional brokerage” is given based on the following parameters: 
 Scenario 1 
 Large Transaction Volume : A broker 
 may receive additional brokerage for handling a high volume of transactions 
 or for exceeding a specific target set by the brokerage firm or client. 
 Scenario 2 
 Exceptional Performance to Meet Specific 
 Targets : Brokers who demonstrate exceptional performance, such as 
 consistently achieving high sales, providing outstanding customer service, 
 or acquiring a particular number of new accounts, may be rewarded with 
 additional brokerage as an incentive. This serves as a motivation and 
 reward for successful outcomes. 
 Scenario 3 
 Complex Transactions : Brokers 
 who successfully handle complex transactions, such as mergers and acquisitions, 
 may receive additional compensation for their expertise and specialized 
 skills. 
 P.S.: It is important to note that the 
 provision of additional brokerage to brokers is subject to the policies 
 and regulations of the firm, as well as any relevant standards and legal 
 requirements. 
 Steps 
 to insert Additional Brokerage into a New Broker Account 
 1 . 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and 
 Customer Care> Booking> Booking 
 2. 2. 
 Navigate to the Broker Info 
 tab and add a new “Broker” from the Add New Row option. 
 1. 3. 
 After creating a new profile, select it and 
 view the option AdditionalAmt 
 in the Broker 
 Info window. Now enter the additional brokerage manually. 
 P.S: 
 The amount needs to be calculated from the given basic value and inserted. 
 4. Once done, click on Save and the details will be set permanently 
 for that broker belonging to that specific Business Unit. 
 Steps to insert 
 Additional Brokerage into an Existing Broker Account 
 1. 1. In the Sales and Customer Care 
 module, select the option which says Brokerage Updation 
 Against Booking under the Brokerage option. 
 (Sales and Customer Care> Brokerage> 
 Brokerage Updation Against Booking) 
 2. Fill in the details marked in red. 
 These include Business Unit, Document Type, Booking No, and Financial 
 Year. Once done, this window will appear. 
 1. 3. 
 Choose the agent for whom “Additional Brokerage” needs to be provided. 
 Upon selection, the Broker Info window will pop-up where AdditionalAmt 
 needs to be inserted manually . 
 P.S . : 
 Note that the Net Amt. has changed. 
 4. Click on Save. 
 Observe that both the Additional Amt and Net Amt are visible 
 now.

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Bulk Proforma Invoice
text:
Bulk Proforma Invoice 
 Help > Transaction > Bulk Transactions" />
 Bulk 
 Proforma Invoice 
 Bulk Proforma Invoice refers to the creation of multiple proforma 
 invoices at once, typically for multiple customers. A proforma invoice 
 is a preliminary bill of sale sent to property buyers before the actual 
 completion of any transaction, outlining the costs and terms of a potential 
 purchase agreement. 
 Why Use Bulk Proforma Invoice? 
 This feature allows businesses to efficiently 
 generate and manage multiple proforma invoices simultaneously, streamlining 
 the invoicing process and saving time. This functionality is beneficial 
 for organisations serving numerous customers at once. 
 Use Case 
 Suppose a property management company 
 needs to generate proforma invoices for multiple owners on a recurring 
 basis based on the completed milestones for that specific project. 
 With the Bulk Proforma Invoice 
 functionality, the property management company can easily generate and 
 distribute proforma invoices to all the owners at once, streamlining the 
 billing process and ensuring that all owners receive accurate and timely 
 invoices. This automation reduces the administrative burden on the property 
 management staff and minimises the possibility of errors that could occur 
 when handling a large volume of invoices manually. 
 Additionally, this feature provides 
 the company with better control and visibility into the invoicing process, 
 allowing them to track and manage payments more efficiently. 
 Steps to Generate Bulk Proforma Invoice 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Sales and Customer 
 Care> Bulk Transactions> Bulk Proforma Invoice. The following 
 screen would be visible. 
 2. 2. Enter the details such as Business 
 Unit, Financial Year, Document Type (type of document relatable to 
 the particular project), Unbilled Upto (all the invoices which 
 are not sent against the set date). All these fields are mandatory. 
 P.S: The Unbilled Upto field 
 will not work if you choose schedule. 
 P.S: The Hierarchy option allows 
 for segregation of different stages in the project hierarchy. This is 
 done for efficient categorisation so that users don’t get confused with 
 the multiple invoices shown. Example: 
 P.S: The Schedule option allows 
 for segregation of different milestones in the project. This is done for 
 efficient categorisation so that users don’t get confused with the multiple 
 invoices shown. Example: 
 3. 3. 
 After filling in the necessary fields, 
 the screen would look like the following. Click on Next once done. 
 4. 4. 
 Under the Output tab, the following 
 grid will appear. Choose the Customers for whom the invoices will 
 be sent according to the set date. Click on Generate once done. 
 The customers would receive their respective invoices. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Bulk Credit Note
text:
Bulk Credit Note 
 Help > Transaction > Bulk Transactions" />

 Note

 basis not selected (It means

title: Bulk Invoice
text:
Bulk Invoice 
 Help > Transaction > Bulk Transactions" />
 Bulk 
 Invoice 
 Bulk 
 Invoice Interface is used to generate the invoice for multiple Payment 
 Schedule or milestones for multiple 
 customers 
 in one go. Invoices for customers for one or more payment schedules will 
 be generated if they are due for payment. This avoids generating invoices 
 for customers individually as it takes time. Invoices generated from here 
 can be edited/deleted as required from Sales 
 and Customer Care > Invoicing > Invoice . 
 Criteria 
 Business 
 Unit : Select business unit 
 Financial 
 Year : It gets populated, however user can select another as per requirement 
 Document 
 Type : Select the document 
 type . 
 Document 
 Date : The invoice date cannot be lesser than any previously generated 
 invoice. 
 This check can be disabled through on request. 
 All schedules whose expected 
 due date falls 
 on or before this date, will be populated in the grid for processing. 
 Document 
 No : System will generate auto Document Number after saving the transaction. 
 If there is any GST 
 billed in this invoice, then Invoice number cannot 
 be greater than 16 characters. 
 Hierarchy : 
 Select the Hierarchy level. If no level is selected,data for all hierarchy 
 levels for the BU will be populated in the grid. 
 Schedule : 
 All 
 schedules which are linked to this Business Unit will be available for 
 selection. Select the Schedule for which the invoices need to be generated. 
 If no schedule is selected, invoices will be generated for all schedules, 
 provided the schedule is due for invoicing. 
 Floor 
 No : Select the floor number 
 Due Date : The due date is the date 
 by which payment of the invoice is due. The due date can be same as the 
 document date or greater than document date. It cannot be is lesser than 
 the document date. Grace period, if any, will apply on top of this due 
 date. 
 Grace 
 Period : Enter the grace period if any. 
 Interest will be calculated from the day after Grace period has been added 
 to the Due Date. 
 Narration : Enter 
 narration if any. 
 Tax 
 Type : Choose any one type of revenue head for which invoice is to 
 be generated - taxable or non-taxable revenue heads. Taxable and non-taxable 
 revenue heads cannot be billed in a single invoice. Separate invoices 
 have to be generated for all taxable and non-taxable revenue heads falling 
 under the selected payment schedule. 
 Click 
 the Next button to populate data for which invoices can be generated. 
 Output 
 Select 
 the multiple customer(s) and click on the Generate button. 
 Only those invoices whose booking 
 date is earlier than the invoice date are displayed here. This is being 
 mentioned because sometimes invoices are generated in back date. 
 If there is any advance received 
 from the customer for which GST has been paid, it will be auto adjusted 
 in the invoice and tax paid in advance will be debited. 
 Customers 
 whose Demand is on Hold, their data will be populated but their invoice 
 will not be generated. 
 Booking 
 amendment is not approved and in provisional stage, the data will be populated 
 but their invoice will not be generated. 
 Selected customer/payment 
 schedules will be filtered and shown in the grid. Once user confirms, 
 the invoices will be generated. 
 Log 
 Log window shows the total success & failure 
 count. 
 In the Advanced 
 Search for Sales 
 and customer care > Invoicing > Invoice , the bulk generated 
 invoices can be seen through Invoice. User can view details, print invoices 
 or send Email, SMS. 
 1. Option incorporated in the 
 Bulk Invoice Error Log to show the Log details against each successful 
 as well as failed invoice generation. 
 Now users will be able to view the entire log 
 details in Bulk Invoice generation against each successful as well as 
 failed invoice generation. 
 Post the 
 bulk invoicing process completion, review the log details. Ensure that 
 log details are displayed for each record chosen for bulk invoicing. 
 For 
 successful generation of an invoice 
 for a selected record, the generated invoice document number is shown 
 against the record under the " Message " 
 column. 
 In 
 the event of a failure to generate the invoice for a selected record, 
 a user-friendly message or reason is displayed against that specific record 
 under the " Message " 
 column. 
 Validate 
 that the counts of success and failure 
 correspond accurately with the number of successful and failed records 
 processed during the bulk invoicing operation . 
 2. Facility incorporated to generate 
 Bulk Invoice through Scheduler process. 
 Step1: Go to the Sales and 
 Customer Care module’s home page. 
 Step2: Navigate to Bulk 
 Transaction and select Bulk Invoice. 
 Step3: Select Business Unit, 
 Financial Year, Document Type, Document Date, Hierarchy, Schedule Name, 
 Due Date, Grace Period, Tax Type. 
 Step4: Proceed by clicking 
 on "Next". 
 Step5: Select "All 
 customers" and initiate the generation process by clicking on "Generate". 
 Step6: Confirm the action 
 by clicking "Yes" and verify that the system displays a message 
 indicating "Process Queued Successfully". 
 Step7: Allow some time for 
 processing. 
 Step8: Access the Queue 
 Management Console and navigate to Process. 
 Step9: Verify that the Bulk 
 Invoice process has been completed. 
 Step10: Confirm that the 
 system displays counts of Total Invoices processed versus Counts of Successful 
 Invoices versus Counts of Errors encountered during the bulk invoicing 
 process. 
 NOTE: 
 This feature needs to be activated through backend and to activate this 
 feature client needs to get help from Gamut Support Team by creating a 
 Query id in Gamut CRM Portal. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Bulk Grace Period
text:
Bulk Grace Period 
 Help > Transaction > Bulk Transactions" />
 Bulk Grace 
 Period 
 If any grace period 
 has not been defined earlier or grace has to be extended for a Payment 
 Schedule or Customer, it can be done in bulk from here. Grace period can 
 be defined in the invoice. This interface will not show any data for which 
 invoice has not been generated. 
 Enhancement 
 of grace period is normally used if there is a delay of delivery or to 
 account for exceptional circumstance (example Covid pandemic). Grace period 
 matters only if there is Late Payment Fee applicable. 
 If 
 partial payment has been received against an invoice, then grace period 
 for that invoice cannot be updated. 
 Criteria 
 Business 
 Unit : Select business unit 
 Hierarchy : Select the Hierarchy 
 if not selected all hierarchy data will show in output window for updated 
 the grace period (Data comes from Sales 
 and Customer Care > Setup > Project > Project Hierarchy ) 
 From 
 Date : Enter starting date from which 
 invoices will be displayed. 
 To Date : 
 Select to date. Invoices will show in 
 the output window for the selected date 
 range only. 
 Schedule: 
 Select 
 the Schedule for which the grace needs 
 to be updated. If no s chedule 
 is selected then invoices for all schedules for the above defined date 
 range will appear for grace period update. 
 Customer: 
 Select a customer. If no customer is selected, 
 invoices for all customers 
 will appear in the output window 
 for the selected date range and schedule. 
 Click 
 on Next button to generate the list of invoices for which grace period 
 has to be updated. 
 Output 
 Here invoices for the selected Payment 
 Schedule and selected Customer will be populated based upon the selected 
 date range. 
 Select 
 the multiple customer(s) invoice or required once as per requirement. 
 Grace Period: Enter the 
 grace period as period requirement. Late payment fee will be calculated 
 from the day after the grace period ends. 
 Due Date: Due date also 
 can be updated. New due date will be updated against the selected invoices 
 only if no payment not received against them. 
 Click 
 on Updated button to update data. After successful updation, dialog box 
 will open, click on OK. 
 After 
 updation, updated grace period and/or due date can be checked in Invoice 
 summary and detail register 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: LPF Process
text:
LPF Process 
 Help > Transaction > Bulk Transactions" />
 LPF Process 
 Days count in Late Payment Fee - Logic for Days 
 count has been corrected for Late Payment Fee calculation 
 Now 
 system will consider the LPF Start and End Date (From date/To Date) correctly 
 in LPF Calculation. Earlier there was a glitch in days count and system 
 was considering 1 day less while calculating LPF against the customer 
 outstanding. Now the same has been corrected and system will calculate 
 the days count correctly. 
 For example: 
 From 
 date=01/04/2019 
 To 
 date= 31/03/2020 
 From 
 and including: 1-April-2019 
 To, 
 but it is not including 31-March-2020 
 Result=365 
 Days 
 As 
 a result, it is 365 days from the start date to the end date, but not 
 including the end date. 
 Now the correction has been made in the days count 
 of LPF Calculation and system will consider the end date as well in the 
 LPF Calculation, therefore as per the above example system will calculate 
 the LPF for 366 days. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited
